sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Western blot confirmed expression of myc-tagged mIFNAR1 (L2); type I IFN signaling via the myc-tagged IFNAR1 / HA-tagged IFNAR2 receptor pair was demonstrated in functional assays (L3) — function preserved.
sites.rationale: L1 explicitly places a myc tag before aa 27 of murine IFNAR1 (the mature N-terminus of the ortholog) in a full-length membrane-anchored receptor. Human IFNAR1 has a 27-aa signal peptide (landmarks), so the analogous junction is after residue 27 (G) and before residue 28 (K), computed from the numbered sequence. This is the sole extracellular terminus of this single-pass receptor, making topology_derived the correct position_evidence. L2 and L3 together confirm both surface expression and preserved IFN signaling, supporting surface_and_function validation. Bicistronic construct encoding full-length, membrane-anchored murine IFNAR1 (P33896 aa 27–590) with a myc tag prepended to the mature extracellular N-terminus, expressed in transfected cells alongside HA-tagged mIFNAR2. The murine signal peptide ends at aa 26, so aa 27 is the mature N-terminus and the tag precedes it. For human IFNAR1 (P17181), the signal peptide ends at aa 27 (mature N-terminus = aa 28), placing the analogous junction at insert_after_residue 27. IFNAR1 is a single-pass type I receptor with exactly one extracellular terminus, so this is the only surface N-terminal position.

sources.claim: The cDNA was generated by fusion of coding sequences for human IL-11R signal peptide (SP; Q14626 , aa 1–24) followed by sequences for HA tag (YPYDVPDYA), murine IFNAR2 ( O35664 , aa 22–513), furin cleavage site (RAKR) followed by sequence for F2A peptide ( Fang et al., 2005 ), coding sequences for human IL-11R SP, myc tag (EQKLISEEDL) and murine IFNAR1 ( P33896 , aa 27–590).

literature_notes: L4 and L5 describe a domain-swap construct (VG mIFNAR1/hIFNAR1) in which the entire extracellular domain is replaced by an anti-GFP nanobody fused to the IFNAR1 TM and cytoplasmic segments (human S422–V557); this is not a tag insertion and does not qualify. L6 and L7 describe a humanized knock-in chimera (human ECD + mouse TM/cytoplasmic) also disqualified as a domain swap. The only qualifying insertion is the myc tag at the N-terminus of the mature extracellular domain of murine IFNAR1 (L1), supported by expression (L2) and functional (L3) data. Evidence is indirect (murine ortholog) so confidence is medium rather than high; the N-terminal extracellular position is nonetheless unambiguous given the single-pass topology.
